officialTitle: Charter Changes Affecting Various City Departments and Commissions
plainEnglish: Charter amendment that would align the Charter with how some City departments currently operate, change some processes, and eliminate or reorganize certain commissions and advisory bodies.
yes: If you vote "yes," you want to amend the Charter to align it with how some City departments currently operate, change some processes, eliminate or reorganize certain commissions and advisory bodies, and require the Board of Supervisors to amend voter-approved laws to enact some of these changes.
no: If you vote "no," you do not want to make these changes.

plainEnglish: Charter amendment that would increase the requirements to put measures on the ballot. The Board of Supervisors could still place measures on the ballot by majority vote.
yes: If you vote "yes," you want to increase the requirements for signature initiatives from 2% to 8% of registered voters (currently from about 10,600 to about 42,500 signatures), increase the requirements for special elections, allow signature initiatives to be withdrawn, and remove the ability of a minority of Board members or the Mayor to place measures on the ballot.
no: If you vote "no," you do not want to make these changes.

shortTitle: Regional transit sales tax (Public Transit Revenue Measure)
measureType: Initiative; district transactions and use (sales) tax
threshold: a simple majority (more than 50%) of votes
ballotQuestion: To prevent major service cuts to BART and other transit, avoid increased traffic, and reduce pollution by: Preserving BART, Caltrain, VTA, SamTrans, AC Transit, Muni, other transit for everyone, including workers, students, seniors, persons with disabilities; Supporting transit safety, cleanliness, affordability, reliability; Repairing targeted roads/potholes; Requiring financial transparency, oversight, accountability; shall the measure enacting a 0.5% (Alameda, Contra Costa, San Mateo, Santa Clara counties), and 1% (San Francisco) sales tax for 14 years generating approximately $980,000,000 annually, be adopted?

plainEnglish: Adds a 0.5% sales tax in Alameda, Contra Costa, San Mateo and Santa Clara counties and a 1% sales tax in San Francisco for 14 years. The ballot question says the money would preserve BART, Caltrain, VTA, SamTrans, AC Transit, Muni and other transit, support transit safety, cleanliness, affordability and reliability, and repair targeted roads and potholes.
yes: A YES vote approves the regional sales tax for 14 years, at 0.5% in Alameda, Contra Costa, San Mateo and Santa Clara counties and 1% in San Francisco.
no: A NO vote rejects the tax.
fiscal: About $980,000,000 per year across the five-county district for 14 years (official ballot question; Alameda County ROV memo to Board of Supervisors, Sept 15, 2026). Alameda County's own share is not stated in the official documents reviewed.
